content: The diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) have been a subject of global discussion, with particular focus on the differences between the one-step and two-step methods. According to the American Diabetes Association (ADA), pregnancies in which GDM was diagnosed using the International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) one-step criteria, but not identified by the traditional two-step method, exhibit health outcomes comparable to those diagnosed using the two-step approach. This observation implies that the one-step diagnostic method may identify cases of GDM that are overlooked by the two-step method. Consequently, the one-step approach could potentially facilitate improved management of GDM and lead to better maternal and neonatal health outcomes.
